U. s. relations with Australia, extremely close during the war, now may become even closer. The Aus tralian government has formally proposed military alliance with the United States.

 In some respects this would make Australia more of a partner to Uncle Sam than to Jol,n Bull, which was virtually the case during the war. For Australian External Minister Herbert Evatt spent most of his time in Washington rather than in London urging more con- centration of U. s. military power in the far east. Simultaneously Prime Minister Churchill spent his time in Washington urging more concentration of U. s. military power in Europe.

 Today history is repeating. Prime Minister Attlee is urging the Uni ted States to keep out of China, withdraw from Korea and concen- trate on Europe; while Australia is urging us to watch China.

 External Minister Percy Spencer has told the American Embassy in Canberra that he hopes the new alliance can. be concluded this year.
